title: Basic Silent Letters (KN, WR, MB, GN)
objectives: Suppress silent initial K, W, G and final B

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Present the pronunciation/reading rule for: Basic Silent Letters (KN, WR, MB, GN). Use the 14 Gabarit fields to clarify rule, system, logic, and exceptions.

teacherNotes.title: Anticipated Problems & Solutions (CELTA Standard)
teacherNotes.content:
⚠️ Problem: Learner pronounces 'climb' as /klaɪmb/ with hard b.
💡 Solution: Cover the letter b with finger during reading drill.

elements.content: Gabarit 14 Champs: Basic Silent Letters (KN, WR, MB, GN)
1. Definition: Consonants that are written in spelling but completely silent in modern pronunciation.
2. Rule: KN- = /n/ (know); WR- = /r/ (write); -MB = /m/ (climb); GN- = /n/ (gnat).
3. Why? These letters were pronounced in Old/Middle English and preserved in spelling after sound loss.
4. How to recognize? Word-initial kn-, wr-, gn- and word-final -mb.
5. Common examples: know /noʊ/, knee /niː/, knife /naɪf/, write /raɪt/, wrong /rɒŋ/, climb /klaɪm/, lamb /læm/, thumb /θʌm/
6. Counter-examples: MB inside words where B starts next syllable (number /nʌmbər/).
7. Exceptions: Subtle /sʌtəl/ (latinate silent b).
8. Common mistakes: Pronouncing the K in 'knee' or B in 'climb'.
9. Mnemonic / Hint: KN = K is sleeping! WR = W is sleeping! MB = B is sleeping at the end!
10. Key vocabulary: silent letter, Germanic origin, initial consonant, final consonant, cluster reduction
11. Frequency: ★★★★☆ (High)
12. CEFR Level: 🟢 A1
13. Associated Visual: 😴 Sleeping letter icon over K in KN, W in WR, B in MB.
14. Key Takeaway: KN=N, WR=R, MB=M. Never pronounce the silent letter!

teacherNotes.title: Teacher CCQ Script
teacherNotes.content: Ask these concept checking questions to verify rule understanding without translation:

elements.content: Rule Understanding Check (CCQ):
CCQ 1: Do you pronounce the K in 'knife'? (No, it is silent)
CCQ 2: Do you pronounce the B at the end of 'climb'? (No, -mb at word end = silent b)
CCQ 3: What sound does WR- make in 'write'? (/r/ sound)

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Auditory discrimination, minimal pairs, and guided oral drill repetition.

elements.content: Read these words without pronouncing the silent letters:
🎯 Item: knee ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: /niː/
🎯 Item: write ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: /raɪt/
🎯 Item: thumb ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: /θʌm/
